newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Rains fail to douse Ukraine grain hopes -trade.
newsitem.headline: Rains fail to douse Ukraine grain hopes -trade.

text.p: Ukraine's hopes for a robust grain harvest this year will probably be fulfilled despite recent heavy rains, traders said on Thursday.

"For the moment, the government figure of 35 million tonnes is still true," said one Western trader. "Some people are a bit more optimistic and have said 40 million tonnes. It will be between 35 and 40 million."

Agriculture Minister Mykhailo Zubets told a news conference Ukraine was optimistic it would get a 35 million tonne harvest since yields were much higher than last year, when drought resulted in a poor outturn of 25.4 million tonnes.

SovEcon Limited, an independent research group, has raised its Ukrainian grain harvest forecast to 37-39 million tonnes following what it said were favourable weather conditions in the past two months.
But the trader said rains that had swept Ukraine could damage output in the country, which regularly produced 50-million-tonne harvests in Soviet times.
"Everyone is afraid because of the weather at the moment," he said. "If the grain is wet it will make it difficult to store."
Zubets, also deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, admitted heavy soil moisture due to rains was slowing down harvesting, which has started in the south.
"By now we should have gathered one million tonnes of grain but we only have 300,000 tonnes," he said.
The minister previously forecast grain exports this year at six million tonnes compared to three million tonnes from the 1996 harvest.

Ukraine's agriculture sector has not yet implemented significant reforms since independence from Moscow in 1991, and it remains heavily dependent on state subsidies. It suffers from major shortages of seeds, fuel and machine parts.
Zubets said Ukraine expected a "much better" barley crop this year than last year's 5.7 million tonnes, although he did not give a figure.
SovEcon forecast barley production at 8.1 million tonnes.
Zubets said Ukraine would increase planting of winter wheat later this year and sunflower seeds next year.
Ukraine has forecast a 1997 sunflower seed harvest of three million tonnes against 2.3 million tonnes.
